utterances.text: Well, I've already said, I don't know her name.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Did you say that she was from the Serbian Radical Party?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO BARICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's what I said.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And what could a woman from the Serbian Radical Party do from Ruma, coming from Ruma to assist the refugees in Hrtkovci?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO BARICEVIC
utterances.text: Well, that's why people demanded that Seselj should come.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Divna Icitovic came from Ruma. She was the president of the Ruma municipality; is that right? Did you hear her name?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO BARICEVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: How could you, an official of the local commune, not know who the president of your municipality was?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO BARICEVIC
utterances.text: Well, you said it now. I don't know who it was. I said that in my statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Well, I didn't know that. My investigators found that out. But you had to know that because you lived in the Ruma municipality, you were an official in the local commune, and by its very nature, the local commune must work closely together with the municipality. And since you encountered those big problems in Hrtkovci, Divna Icitovic, the president of the Ruma municipality, came to Hrtkovci and tried to calm down the situation, to talk to the refugees to find some kind of a solution; is that so?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO BARICEVIC
utterances.text: I don't know what it is that she talked about. I know that people asked yet again to have a meeting.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Did I come to the meeting?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have a question for the witness. This lady who came from Ruma, is it the same lady as the one who took part in the demonstration on May 6th, in the rally on May 6th when Mr. Seselj came?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I've said -- well, at this first meeting when she came with the Radicals, I was not there. I don't know the woman. I mean, I cannot make a comparison. Was she the one who came, or was it a different person?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, you were there when Mr. Seselj delivered his speech. First, Mr. Zilic took the floor. After Mr. Zilic, a lady spoke. This lady is Marica Pacinin.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I stated that I did not know the woman's name. That's what I said in my statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now, Mr. Seselj is telling us that the lady who came from Ruma is called Divna Icitovic. She came before May 6th. So before May 6th, Divna Icitovic comes to Hrtkovci, but then on May 6th, we have Pacinin also. So we have two ladies coming from Ruma. Is that possible, impossible, or is it the same lady?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I said that I was not at the first meeting, so I don't know. I mean --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You don't know. Very well. Proceed.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But the witness is testifying as if he did know, as if he were there, and he claims that this was a meeting with the activists of the Serb Radical Party. I'd just like to draw your attention to that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Now, hypothetically, the refugees are asking for me to come to the meeting. I come and I speak at a rally. Is a rally the same thing as a meeting?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO BARICEVIC
utterances.text: No, no. That was a rally.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Did anybody talk to me? Could anybody talk to me, or was I the only one who spoke and who shook hands with people, got into a car and went to Belgrade? Could anybody from the audience say anything to me?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO BARICEVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: So that wasn't a meeting, then?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO BARICEVIC
utterances.text: Well, all right. It was a rally.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So there was no meeting.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, here, again, there's something that seems very illogical. If Mr. Seselj comes at the request of the unhappy Serbs that have been expelled from Croatia, then this is what should happen: Mr. Seselj comes, makes a speech, and at least meets those people in order to discuss their problems with them. But it seems he comes by car. We had ample details on this. There was even a flat tyre at one point in time, which -- you know, we know everything about this arrival. He delivers a speech, and then he leaves. Obviously, he did not discuss with these people, so that seems very illogical. If he's coming at the request of the population because he's supposed to solve all the problems, he should at least discuss with these people, but he just comes in a convoy of cars with security details, and then he just leaves. How can you explain this?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is true that he made a speech and that he gave people guidelines as to what they should do. Now, when he finished, I turned around and left. Now, whether he stayed on to talk to people or not, that is something that I really don't know. At any rate, he gave people guidelines as to what it was that they should do.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Should I go on? Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: When I allegedly state from the stage that all children from mixed marriages should be killed, was thunderous applause heard from the masses? Did I experience ovations? How did people take this statement of mine, that children from mixed marriages should be killed?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO BARICEVIC
utterances.text: I don't know how they experienced it. I know that I was horrified when I heard that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Were there any ovations? Was there any applause?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO BARICEVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Were there a lot of women at this rally?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO BARICEVIC
utterances.text: There were quite a few women.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: How did the women react when they heard that I was advocating the killing of children from mixed marriages? Were they thrilled? Were they jumping up and down with joy?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO BARICEVIC
utterances.text: I did not ask them, and I didn't say that they were delighted. I said that I was horrified.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: What did the women around you look like? Were there a lot of children at the rally?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO BARICEVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: How come? At every rally, a lot of children come, especially in smaller towns and villages.

utterances.speaker: FRANJO BARICEVIC
utterances.text: There weren't any children.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: No children?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO BARICEVIC
utterances.text: Well, a few.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: You are inventing this. There were a lot of children. Now, the children who were present, there are a few of them, as you say. Were they thrilled when they heard me advocating the killing of children from mixed marriages?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO BARICEVIC
utterances.text: Well, I did not talk to these children, I mean -- or with the others. I mean, when I heard that, I was horrified and I went home.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: How come --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, you were horrified, and everybody's horrified on hearing such things. It so happens that we heard a witness who came before you. This witness came from a mixed marriage. He had two children. This witness was here -- was there. He heard the speech. He didn't tell us that he'd heard that. How can you explain this, that he didn't hear it and that you heard it? He must have been very concerned if anybody was to be concerned. Can you explain this?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I don't know how come he didn't hear that and how come he didn't say so, but Judge, Your Honour, that was stated at the rally.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We'll stop for now because I need to hand down an oral decision. This may take some time. The Registrar will give us the countdown and tell us how much time Mr. Seselj still has to finish his cross-examination. We shall see each other again, Witness, tomorrow at a quarter past 2.00. So let me renew my instructions to you. You must not contact anyone to discuss your testimony because your testimony is resuming tomorrow. So you're going to be leaving the courtroom so that I can read out the oral decision.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Seselj, at the beginning of the afternoon, you talked to us about the witness's testimony who is due to come after this one. I would not give his name because we have been asked to give him protective measures. This concerns Witness VS-1132. This is the Trial Chamber's oral decision. In light of the motion filed on the 25th of September, 2008, to admit the written statement of Milorad -- of the Witness VS-1134 on the 11th of September, 2008, pursuant to Rule 92 ter; considering the response provided by the accused at the hearing of the 14th of October, 2008; given that in addition the accused on several occasions has clearly indicated that he was opposed to the application of Rule 92 ter of the Rules; considering that the written statement of this witness has to do with the presence of volunteers' units in Vukovar as well as his own presence in Ovcara -- I just need to talk to the legal officer for a few minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have just talked to the legal officer. The name of the witness is Milorad Vosnovic [phoen]. He's not coming tomorrow but on the 6th of November. That is why I needed to check this. Let me resume. Considering that the written statement of this witness has to do with the presence of volunteers' units in Vukovar as well as his own presence in Ovcara; considering that the Trial Chamber holds that this statement is relevant because it relates clearly to events alleged in the indictment; considering, then, with a view to being efficient and quick, pursuant to Rule 92 ter, it is in the interest of justice to allow this witness to come and testify before the Trial Chamber pursuant to Rule 92 ter of the Rules of Procedure and Evidence for the foregoing reasons: (a), the witness Milorad Vosnovic will testify on the 6th of November, 2008, pursuant to Rule 92 ter of the Rules, based on his statement of the 11th of September, 2008; (b), the Trial Chamber decides to grant the Prosecution 30 minutes to fill in the formalities pursuant to Rule 92 ter; (c), the Trial Chamber decides that the accused will have one hour for the cross-examination of this witness; (d), the Trial Chamber decides that the written statement dated the 11th of September, 2008, will only be admitted after the formal criteria contained in Rule 92 ter will have been met. So much for this witness who will come and testify on the 6th of November. Before then - and this is something I need to inform you about, Mr. Seselj, because this is urgent - I wanted to discuss the witness who would be coming before Milorad Vosnovic. This is why you're on your feet, Ms. Dahl?

utterances.speaker: MS. DAHL
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, I'm trying to correlate pseudonyms and full -- correct names of witnesses. Could we go into private session for a moment, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Registrar, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're back in open.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Seselj, I must tell you that a few days ago, the OTP sent us a request, i.e., that Witness Vesna Bosanac be heard pursuant to our 92 ter Rule. This motion was being translated. I don't know whether this motion has been disclosed to you in your language. If it hasn't been disclosed to you, let me tell you that the Prosecution has got a new statement of Vesna Bosanac, and the Prosecutor has asked for this witness to be heard pursuant to 92 ter. That said, the Prosecutor has also allowed enough time for your cross-examination. This is why this woman will be heard over a period of two days. The Trial Chamber would like you to tell us today what your position on this is.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You know that I'm absolutely opposed to the application of Rule 92 ter because this makes the trial unfair and it seriously infringes upon my rights. Secondly, the OTP has wasted an enormous amount of time bringing in crime-base witnesses that have to do with crimes that are no longer in the indictment. That is what they wasted time on, and for those localities that are still in the indictment, they are asking for 92 ter. Even if legally this were to be right, it would be highly irrational in view of the fact that my rights are being violated. As for the application of 92 ter, I don't want to discuss it. It doesn't exist for me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let me tell you this: I have read the 92 ter statement of this witness, Madam Vesna Bosanac, very carefully. In her statement, at no point in time are you mentioned. The members of the SRS are never mentioned. She is going to testify and talk about what happened in the hospital which was shelled, and she will also in her statement talk about everything she did. She turned to the Croatian authorities, and she turned to the JNA. And then she will testify about what happened when the hospital was shelled, captured. So much for the content of her testimony. The Trial Chamber has recorded your comments, and we will let you know and tell you what our decision will be, a decision taken by the entire Bench. Mr. Seselj.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, the situation is very murky as regards Ovcara. You and your colleagues have already been able to see that for yourselves. The Mrksic trial, the trial of Mrksic and the others did not really cast any more light on it. Mrksic was convicted only on the basis of assumptions. There is no information as to who decided to take the prisoners to Ovcara, where there is this record of the hand-over, what is the role of the four colonels of the Security Service who were reactivated although had been retired, and without any papers they were sent to Vukovar. Who decided to execute the prisoners? Who kept silent for months after the execution? Now, as for Colonel Milorad Vojnovic, you allowed him to testify under 92 ter. He was the commander of the town that Ovcara belonged to, and from the 23rd of November onwards, for several months he was the commander of Vukovar. Instead of having him sitting here as an accused person, he comes to testify against me according to 92 ter, against me, who had no idea whatsoever of what it was that was going on over there. If you think that this is the right way to proceed, well, then, fine. You do that until the very end. But he comes to testify against me, and his military police from his brigade was at Ovcara until the very last moment, and they handed over the detainees to the people there without any record. These people were executed, and he comes to testify against me. That is possible too. Well, go ahead and do it that way if that's what you want, but I am not going to question him if his statement is admitted according to Rule 92 ter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Seselj, you are saying that he's coming to testify against you. All the more reason for you to cross-examine him. Under 92 ter, the Prosecution says that there is a statement. I shall ask him to confirm the statement. "I would like such-and-such a document to be tendered into evidence." Then you are free to put your questions. If you don't put your question, I, in any case, will put questions to the witness. These questions need to be put in the interests of justice, and I shall do my job even if you don't say anything. So I have noted what you have said as regards this witness, and the Judges will put their questions. We have the statement, and we check everything, and you must have realised this by now. We're not here to leave some questions unexplained. We are to determine whether you are guilty or innocent, which is a huge responsibility on our shoulders, and we are not entitled to make a mistake. This is why we will put our questions. If you don't put the questions, we will put our questions. Tomorrow, we shall resume. You shall resume your cross-examination. You have, as far as this witness is concerned, one hour and a half left to finish with him. At the end of your cross-examination, there might be a redirect, I don't know, and then we shall hear our next witness. I apologise to the interpreters for having overstepped the Trial Chamber's time by five minutes. I'm sure they will accept this. We shall meet again at a quarter past 2.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Wednesday, the 15th day of October, 2008, at 2.15 p.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 7.05 p.m.,
